items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: In the class I spoke to here at the college we were talking about gender issues in music, and Dr. Woods brought up the fact that what was going on in the music community was reflecting what was going on in the society

ctx.x: Who was trying to control it?

Oh it’s not a who, it’s not any particular person, it was prevalent in, you could see it in the way festivals and the way groups were lining up to play at certain clubs at certain places, and the way they were being recorded too. It’s not a finger pointing thing. It was — you could sense it in the consciousness of what was going on, and it had to do with also the kind of conservativism that had overtaken the music community as well too. I think it went hand in hand with what was going on with it in the country.…
Has the music been affected by the fact that it’s become almost institutionalized, that mostly it’s taught in colleges now as opposed to kind of on the job training?
